dissent: A defender could read the obligation predicate as intentionally scoped to collect-open/collect:/source:; rejected — the docstring, REFUSALS tuple, JUST['attest'], and predict_attest show attestation/inventory is the intended o06 core.
'seen' may be defended as fields-observed-so-far; comparing it at a new obligation event rather than that event's payload still produces wrong verdicts.
findings: CRITICAL dead obligation: `obligation = v == 'collect-open' or v.startswith(('collect:','source:'))` (proposal L259) is never true for v=='source-attest' (hyphen, not colon), so the entire source-attest block (L264-292), predict_attest (L173-186), and the attest arms of the invocation-mask/justification checks (L309, L315) are unreachable. Attestation refusals (s_inclusive.py:63-68; s_audit.py source-attest clause; guard_audit.py same) get no expected-vs-observed decision, Q-invocation, justification, census, or oevents accounting; 'supported'/'not_applicable' can be reported with zero inventory verification. Minimal fix: include `v == 'source-attest'` in the predicate. Counterexample shape: any case whose source-attest row carries a fabricated refusal decision (e.g. 'source-attest:incomplete-inventory' on a complete capture) passes silently.

Prerequisite missing — no o06 control exists. recovered-proposals.json contains only o06-collection-inventory-implement (obligation_checks/collection_inventory.py, sha256 matching reviewed bytes; origin_state 'unknown', origin_error 'Refused: native Linux client did not complete normally'); unlike o05 there is no o06-collection-inventory-control-build. Checker/control interoperability cannot be compared; wave04-required discriminations (false Q invocation on refused attestation, dropped refusal, changed census/observation) are untested and would have exposed finding 1.

Stale-'seen' false positives: capture/sorting witnesses (L321-328) test membership in and compare accumulated `seen`, not the current event's `live` (L319-320). On profiles with two collect-open phases (s_domain.py 'restart-recollect'), if the second open's event does not re-expose 'collection', the first capture tuple is compared against the new expected capture → spurious 'counterexample' (or false pass if identical); same for 'collected' after re-open resets it to (). Minimal fix: key both witnesses off `live`.

Attestation prediction cannot bind the delivered cut: 'cut_delivery' is listed in FIELDS (L54) but never seeded (L103-109) or updated by apply_ok; the check accepts the observed reason whenever ANY fixture candidate predicts it (`reason not in set(preds.values())`, L275-284). A 'success' delivery that should refuse 'incomplete-inventory' is accepted if another fixture predicts the same label; a capture-present/no-delivery attestation (actual 'no-captured-source') is never in preds → false mismatch. Currently dead under finding 1 but must be fixed together: project cut_delivery and compare the single delivered cut's prediction.
